# Caldera - full text

## Turn your GitHub into a living city
URL: https://caldera.social/github-profile-city

Sign up at caldera.social with GitHub and Caldera builds a city from your repos in about 30 seconds, with nothing to install. Each building is a repo, its height grows with your commits over the last year, and windows light up for repos you committed to this week. The city sits on a public profile page that rebuilds from GitHub every 6 hours, and it can show visitors to your sites and your AI agents live.

### What you get
A city of your repos. Buildings are repos and districts group them. Public repos are named and link to GitHub. Private repos, your way. Install the Caldera GitHub app on the repos you choose. By default they appear as padlocked buildings with no names; switch to anonymous (one separate padlocked district) or hidden in Settings. The app has read-only access to repository metadata and cannot open your files. Live visitors. Add one script tag to a site and its visitors parachute into your city as they arrive; signups and sales get their own celebrations. AI agents as drones. A small hook shows your coding agents over the repo they are working in. The time of day. The sky follows the viewer's clock, from dawn to night. Pop the city out into a small window and watch it all day. People. Follow builders (follow each other and you are friends), message them, post on the Feed , start a group at caldera.social/g/name, and get a daily summary by email.

### How to do it
Go to caldera.social/auth/github and sign in with GitHub. Your page is built and filled in for you: nothing to fill out. Your page and city are built from your public repos and open on your account page. Edit your name, headline, links and photo there, add private repos if you want them, and copy the live-visitor snippet for your sites.

### Use Obsidian too?
Move your GitHub sign-up into an Obsidian vault any time and keep your page. Your vault adds a daily journal, AI usage and end-to-end encrypted sharing with friends. Already on Obsidian? Add your GitHub link to Caldera/profile.md and Caldera builds your city from your public repos. See What is Caldera?

### Questions
Q: Does Caldera read my code?
A: No. It reads repo names, languages, sizes, commit counts and your public activity. The optional GitHub app for private repos has read-only access to repository metadata, which does not include file contents.
Q: Is it free?
A: Yes. Your page, your city and friends are free, and the code is open source.
Q: How do I delete it?
A: On your account page, choose Delete my Caldera profile. Your page is erased and Caldera's access to your GitHub is revoked.

## What is Caldera?
URL: https://caldera.social/what-is-caldera

Caldera is a free, open-source social network for GitHub and Obsidian. Sign up with GitHub and your repos become a living city: districts are projects, buildings are repos, and visitors to your sites and your AI agents move through it live. Install the Obsidian plugin and your vault becomes a living public profile. Members follow each other (mutual follows are friends), message each other, post what they need or recommend on the Feed, join groups and share notes end-to-end encrypted. It is private by default

### What Caldera does
GitHub city. Sign up with GitHub and your public repos become a city at caldera.social/@you/city.html, rebuilt every 6 hours. Private repos appear only if you install the Caldera GitHub app, as padlocked buildings with no names. Living profile. With Obsidian, a public page built on your own device from your vault and republished automatically. Follow and friends. Follow anyone; when you follow each other you are friends. Friends can share any note as an end-to-end encrypted card that lands in their vault as a normal note. Feed and messages. Post "I need..." or "I recommend..." and it reaches the people who match. Message members directly; strangers send a request first. Kudos and views. One-tap kudos and a view count on every page. AI-native setup. One copy-paste prompt lets Claude Code, Codex or Cursor install it and run a daily journal routine.

### Who makes it
Caldera is built by mjonesone, LLC. The plugin and core library are MIT-licensed, the reference hub is AGPL-3.0 and self-hostable, and the protocol is open. Source: github.com/schoettle-cmd/caldera .

### How private is it?
The plugin reads your vault locally and never uploads it. Only counts, the profile sections you switch on, notes you mark caldera: public , and journal fields you write are published. Shared notes are end-to-end encrypted; the hub stores ciphertext it cannot read. Your identity is a key in your vault, not a password account.

### Questions
Q: Is Caldera free?
A: Yes. The plugin, your profile and friends are free and open source.
Q: Does Caldera need Obsidian?
A: No. Sign up with GitHub and you get a page and a city with nothing to install. Obsidian adds a living profile, a journal and AI usage, and a GitHub sign-up can move into a vault any time.
Q: Is Caldera an official Obsidian or GitHub product?
A: No. Caldera is an independent, open-source project made by mjonesone, LLC.

## How to make a public profile from your Obsidian vault
URL: https://caldera.social/obsidian-public-profile

The fastest way to turn an Obsidian vault into a public profile page is the free Caldera plugin: install it (or paste one prompt into Claude Code, Codex or Cursor and let the AI install it), type your name and a handle in the Welcome window, and your page goes live at caldera.social/@yourhandle. It rebuilds itself from your vault, publishing only counts and the notes and sections you switch on.

### Steps
Install Obsidian if you don't have it (free at obsidian.md ). Copy the setup prompt from caldera.social/#install into your AI agent, or install the plugin by hand from the latest release. Open Obsidian. The Welcome to Caldera window asks for your name and a handle, creates your identity on your device, publishes your page and opens it in your browser. Edit the note Caldera/profile.md to change your headline, photo, links, projects and which sections show. The page republishes about a minute after you save.

### What can be on the page
A flippable daily journal, an activity score and 26-week heatmap, a growth chart, your public topics, projects, a timeline, links, AI usage charts, and any note you mark caldera: public (title and first paragraph). Every section has an on/off switch. See a full example: caldera.social/@mike .

### What stays private
Note contents stay on your computer unless you mark a note public. Topics are allow-listed, so only tags you approve are counted, and the plugin publishes counts rather than titles. You can preview before publishing and delete your page with one command.

### Questions
Q: Can I use my own domain?
A: You can export your profile as a static site and host it anywhere, or run your own Caldera hub.
Q: Does it update automatically?
A: Yes. It republishes every few hours and about a minute after you edit Caldera/profile.md.
Q: Do I need to code?
A: No. Paste one prompt into an AI agent, or install the plugin by hand and use the Welcome window.

## How to share Obsidian notes privately with friends
URL: https://caldera.social/share-obsidian-notes-privately

To share a single Obsidian note privately, use the free Caldera plugin: add a friend by their handle, open the note and run "Caldera: Share this note with a friend". The note is encrypted on your device so only that friend can read it, and it arrives in their vault as a normal Markdown note under Caldera/Inbox. Nothing is posted publicly and the server only stores ciphertext.

### How it works
Both of you install Caldera and pick a handle. Send a friend request from the Caldera panel (the flame icon); your friend accepts it. On any note, run Share this note with a friend from the command palette. Your friend's vault receives the note on its next sync, in Caldera/Inbox/your-handle/ .

### Other ways to share Obsidian notes
Obsidian Sync shared vaults (paid): share a whole vault with collaborators. Obsidian Publish (paid) or static-site tools: public pages, not private sharing. Collaboration plugins : shared folders edited live by a team. Caldera (free): one note at a time to one friend, end-to-end encrypted, landing in their own vault.

### Questions
Q: Can the server read shared notes?
A: No. Notes are encrypted on your device with your friend's public key; the hub stores ciphertext only.
Q: Does my friend need Obsidian?
A: Yes, shared notes are delivered into an Obsidian vault with Caldera installed.
Q: Can I unshare a note?
A: A delivered note is a copy in your friend's vault, like an email. You can stop sharing future versions.

## Is there a social network for Obsidian users?
URL: https://caldera.social/obsidian-social-network

Yes. Caldera is an open-source social layer built for Obsidian: every member gets a living profile generated from their vault, members follow each other (mutual follows are friends) and share end-to-end encrypted notes, post what they need or recommend on the Feed, and a People directory at caldera.social/people lets you browse profiles by what people work on.

### How it differs from a normal social network
Your vault is the source. Profiles are built from your own notes on your own device, not typed into a website. Private by default. Only the sections and notes you switch on are published. Open protocol. Identity is a key in your vault; the hub is open source and self-hostable. Built for finding people. Feed posts reach the members who match what you need, not an engagement-ranked timeline.

### Where Obsidian users talk today
The official Obsidian forum and Discord, and the r/ObsidianMD subreddit, are where the community discusses the app. Caldera complements them: it is about connecting vaults and showing your work, not discussion threads.

### Questions
Q: How do I find other Obsidian users on Caldera?
A: Browse caldera.social/people and search by name, headline or topic.
Q: Can I stay unlisted?
A: Yes. Turn off "List me in the directory" and your page works only for people with the link.
Q: How do I invite friends?
A: Use "Invite a friend" on your page's leaderboard, or share caldera.social/?invite=yourhandle.

## Free alternatives to Obsidian Publish
URL: https://caldera.social/obsidian-publish-alternatives

Obsidian Publish is the official paid way to put a vault online as a website. Popular free alternatives are Quartz (an open-source static-site generator for publishing many notes), digital-garden style community plugins that publish selected notes to hosts like Netlify or Vercel, and Caldera, which publishes a living profile page about you and your work rather than your notes themselves. Pick by goal: a full notes website, a curated garden, or a profile that updates itself.

### Comparison
Option Cost Best for Setup Obsidian Publish Paid add-on (see obsidian.md for current pricing) An official, hosted website of your notes Built into Obsidian Quartz Free, open source A full static site of many notes, self-hosted Command line + a static host Digital-garden plugins Free (hosting tier dependent) Publishing selected notes as a garden Plugin + Netlify/Vercel account Caldera Free, open source A living profile: journal, activity, projects, chosen notes, plus friends and private sharing One prompt or the plugin; hosted at caldera.social or self-hosted

### When Caldera is the right choice
Choose Caldera if you want a page that shows what you're working on and updates itself, while your actual notes stay private, and if you want to connect with other Obsidian users. If you want to publish hundreds of notes as a browsable website, use Obsidian Publish or Quartz; Caldera can link to it.

### Questions
Q: Can I use Caldera and Quartz together?
A: Yes. Many people publish a notes site with Quartz or Publish and use Caldera for their profile, linking the two.
Q: Does Caldera publish my whole vault?
A: No. It publishes counts, sections you turn on, and only notes marked caldera: public (title and first paragraph).
Q: Is there a hosting cost?
A: Profiles on caldera.social are free. Self-hosting the open-source hub is also possible.

## Using Claude Code, Codex or Cursor with Obsidian
URL: https://caldera.social/obsidian-ai-agent-setup

Because an Obsidian vault is just a folder of Markdown files, AI coding agents like Claude Code, OpenAI Codex and Cursor can work in it directly: install plugins, edit notes, and run daily routines. Caldera ships copy-paste prompts built for this: one installs Obsidian (if needed) and the Caldera plugin, then has the agent write your daily journal and activity counts each morning under strict privacy rules, and never lets it touch your identity key.

### The three Caldera prompts
Setup ( caldera.social/#install ): install Obsidian and Caldera, then a daily journal + activity routine. Make it richer ( caldera.social/#richer ): suggests public notes, topics, activity sources and a 14-day journal backfill, asking before anything goes public. Change my profile ( caldera.social/guide ): describe a change in plain English; the agent edits Caldera/profile.md and the page republishes.

### Safety rules built into the prompts
Privacy rules override everything: no names, clients, money, health, family or locations on public pages. Anything that would become public needs your explicit yes. The agent never reads or edits the plugin's key file, so your identity key never passes through the model.

### Questions
Q: Which AI agents work?
A: Any agent that can read and write files on your computer: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, and similar tools.
Q: Can the AI run this daily?
A: Yes. The setup prompt describes a once-a-day routine you can schedule with your agent.
Q: Does the AI see my private key?
A: No. The prompts forbid reading the plugin's data.json, and your identity is created by the plugin, not the AI.

## An automatic daily journal in Obsidian, written by AI
URL: https://caldera.social/obsidian-daily-journal-ai

You can have an AI agent write a short journal entry in Obsidian every morning: it reads yesterday's notes, calendar, sent email, commits and AI sessions, then adds a headline, focus, wins and themes to that day's daily note. With the Caldera plugin those entries become a flippable daily journal on your public profile, alongside an activity score, while the privacy rules keep names, clients and money out of anything public.

### What gets written
Four properties on each daily note (named YYYY-MM-DD.md ): caldera_headline (one sentence), caldera_focus (2-4 items), caldera_wins (1-3 items) and caldera_themes (1-3 words). Daily counts (meetings, emails sent, AI prompts, commits, documents) go in Caldera/activity.json .

### How to set it up
Copy the setup prompt from caldera.social/#install into Claude Code, Codex or Cursor. After install, schedule the agent to run the daily routine each morning. Use the "make it richer" prompt to backfill the last 14 days.

### Questions
Q: Do I have to make the journal public?
A: No. The journal section has an on/off switch; the entries stay in your daily notes either way.
Q: What if a day had nothing public to say?
A: The rules allow empty fields; the page shows the activity counts only.
Q: Can I write entries myself?
A: Yes. The same four properties work whether you or an agent write them.

## Track your AI token usage by day and by model
URL: https://caldera.social/track-ai-token-usage

Claude Code and OpenAI Codex both keep local usage logs with the model and token counts for every response, so you can chart your AI usage without any API access. Caldera's prompts have your AI agent total those logs into tokens per day, per model and per provider (counts only, never prompts or costs), and the AI usage section of your profile shows the daily chart and your model mix.

### Where the numbers come from
Claude Code: ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl - assistant messages include message.model and message.usage (input, output, cache read and cache write tokens). Count each message id once. Codex: ~/.codex/sessions/**/*.jsonl - token_count events carry per-turn usage; the model comes from turn_context .

### What surprises most people
Agent sessions re-read cached context constantly, so totals are dominated by cache reads. On one heavy user's profile, about 7.7 billion tokens over 45 days were almost all cached context. Charting it by model also shows how much work each model actually does.

### Questions
Q: Does this show my costs?
A: No. Only token counts and model names are published; money amounts are deliberately excluded.
Q: Does it read my prompts?
A: No. Only usage fields (model, token counts, timestamps) are totaled.
Q: Which tools are supported?
A: Claude Code and Codex out of the box; any tool that keeps local usage logs can be added by your agent.

## Activity heatmap, streaks and a leaderboard for Obsidian
URL: https://caldera.social/obsidian-activity-tracker

Caldera adds a GitHub-style 26-week activity heatmap, a daily activity score, streaks, your best days and a friends leaderboard to your Obsidian vault, shown on your public profile. The score combines notes written plus optional outside counts (meetings, emails sent, AI prompts, commits, documents), with caps so a bulk import can't win a day.

### What's measured
Notes created and changed each day come from the vault itself. Outside activity comes from Caldera/activity.json , which your AI agent or scripts can fill with counts. Only numbers are published.

### Compete with friends, positively
The leaderboard ranks you against friends by points this week. There are no downvotes, and points come only from your own activity.

### Questions
Q: How is the score calculated?
A: Weighted daily counts (meetings, emails, prompts, commits, notes, documents), each capped so bulk imports can't dominate. The formula is shown on every page under "How the score works".
Q: Can I hide the heatmap?
A: Yes. Every section can be switched off in Caldera/profile.md.
Q: Does it work on mobile?
A: Yes. The plugin runs on Obsidian desktop and mobile, and profiles are responsive.

## GitHub city: your repos as a living city
URL: https://caldera.social/github-city

A GitHub city is a visualization where every repository is a building and related repos form districts, so a developer's body of work reads like a skyline. On Caldera, open caldera.social/gh/<username> to see any public GitHub account as a city, or sign up with GitHub to get a live city that updates itself.

### How a GitHub city reads
Buildings are repos. Height grows with commits over the last year, so the work you actually do stands tallest. Districts group repos. On a member's city a district is a project; on a quick preview it is a language. Lit windows mean commits this week. A crane means a repo is being built right now. Private repos appear only if the owner adds them, as padlocked buildings with no names (or anonymous, or hidden). The sky follows the viewer's clock and local weather, from dawn to night.

### See any GitHub as a city
Go to caldera.social/gh . Type a GitHub username and press See the city . Caldera draws a preview from public data only: public repos, languages and recent commit activity. Previews refresh daily. If the account already belongs to a Caldera member, you go straight to their real city instead.

### Get your own live city
Sign up with GitHub and your city lives on your own page at caldera.social/@you/city.html. It rebuilds from GitHub every 6 hours, shows visitors to your websites as they arrive, and shows your AI coding agents as drones over the repos they are working in. See Turn your GitHub into a living city . Try it on any public GitHub account at caldera.social/gh , or sign up with GitHub to get your own live city.

### A city of cities
Every member's city also sits on one shared map, the World , where friendships show as rays of light between cities.

### Questions
Q: Is a GitHub city free?
A: Yes. Previews and your own city on Caldera are free.
Q: Does Caldera read my code?
A: No. It uses repo names, languages, sizes and commit counts. It never opens file contents.
Q: Why does a preview look smaller than my real work?
A: Previews count the 20 most recently pushed public repos in detail and cannot see organization repos or private work. Your own city can include organization and private repos you add.
Q: Can I remove a preview of my account?
A: Yes. Claim it by signing up with GitHub, or email hello@caldera.social and it is removed.
Q: Does it work for organizations?
A: Not yet. Previews are for personal GitHub accounts.

## How to visualize your GitHub activity
URL: https://caldera.social/visualize-github-activity

The simplest view of GitHub activity is the contribution graph on your profile, which counts contributions per day for a year. To see what you worked on, not just when, use a repo-level view such as a GitHub city on Caldera, where each repo is a building that grows with commits and lights up when it is active this week.

### Four common ways
View Shows Best for Contribution graph (built into GitHub) Contributions per day, last year Consistency at a glance README stats cards Totals, top languages, streaks A quick summary on your profile 3D contribution models A year of contributions as a shape A one-off keepsake A GitHub city (Caldera) Every repo as a building, grouped into districts, live activity Seeing what you build and where you are active now

### Try the city view in 10 seconds
Open caldera.social/gh . Enter your GitHub username. Read the city: tall buildings are your most committed repos this year, lit windows are this week, cranes are being built right now.

### Go further: make it live
Sign up with GitHub and your city becomes a page that updates itself. Add a one-line script to your websites and visitors parachute into the district for that site. Add the Claude Code hook and your coding agents fly over the repos they are editing. See Visualize your AI coding agents .

### Put it on your profile
Add the Caldera badge to your GitHub profile README so visitors can open your city in one click. See GitHub README badge .

### Questions
Q: What is the best way to visualize GitHub activity?
A: Use the contribution graph for consistency and a repo-level view, such as a GitHub city, for what you actually work on.
Q: Can I visualize someone else's GitHub?
A: Yes, from public data: open caldera.social/gh/<username>.
Q: Does it include private repos?
A: Only on your own city, and only if you add them; they appear without names.
Q: How often does it update?
A: Previews refresh daily. Members' cities rebuild from GitHub every 6 hours, and live visitors and agents show in real time.

## An alternative to the GitHub contribution graph
URL: https://caldera.social/github-contribution-graph-alternative

GitHub's contribution graph shows how many contributions you made each day, but not which projects they went into. Caldera's GitHub city is a complementary view: each repo is a building that grows with its commits over the year, districts group related repos, and lit windows show what you touched this week.

### What the contribution graph is good at
The green grid on every GitHub profile is a fast read on consistency: busy days are darker, streaks are visible, and it covers a full year. It counts contributions, so one big week on a side project looks the same as one big week on your main product.

### What a city adds
Where the work went. Each repo is its own building, so your main projects stand out. Shape of a career. Districts group repos into projects (or languages on a preview). Right now. Windows light up for this week's commits and cranes mark repos being built today. Live. On a member's city, website visitors and AI coding agents appear as they happen.

### Side by side
Contribution graph Caldera city Unit Day Repo Window Last 12 months Last 12 months, plus this week and today Private work Optional count Optional, padlocked with no names, or hidden Live activity No Visitors and AI agents

### Try it
Try it on any public GitHub account at caldera.social/gh , or sign up with GitHub to get your own live city.

### Questions
Q: Does Caldera replace the contribution graph?
A: No. It sits alongside it. Many people link their city from their GitHub README.
Q: Will private contributions show?
A: Only if you add private repos to your own city, and never with names.
Q: Is it accurate?
A: Commit counts come from GitHub's own statistics. Previews count the 20 most recently pushed public repos in detail.
Q: Is it free?
A: Yes.

## A GitHub Skyline alternative that stays live
URL: https://caldera.social/github-skyline-alternative

GitHub Skyline turned a year of contributions into a 3D model you could look at or print. If you want something that keeps updating, Caldera turns your repos into a living city: each repo is a building, this week's work lights the windows, and your page refreshes from GitHub on its own.

### Snapshot versus living view
A skyline model is a snapshot of one year of contribution counts. A Caldera city is per repo and keeps changing: it rebuilds from GitHub every 6 hours, the sky follows the viewer's time and weather, and live events (visitors to your sites, your coding agents) appear as they happen.

### What you can do with a city
Share it: every city has a link preview image for X, LinkedIn and chat apps. Embed a badge in your README that opens it. Pop it out into a small window and keep it on screen all day. See it next to everyone else's on the World map.

### Make one now
Open caldera.social/gh and enter your username for an instant preview. Click Claim it with GitHub to turn the preview into your own live city.

### Questions
Q: Can I print my Caldera city?
A: Not as a 3D file today. You can share it, embed it and pop it out on screen.
Q: Is it per year or per repo?
A: Per repo: building height reflects that repo's commits over the last year.
Q: Does it need any install?
A: No. Sign up with GitHub in your browser.
Q: Is it free?
A: Yes.

## Add a GitHub city badge to your README
URL: https://caldera.social/github-readme-badge

Caldera gives every GitHub account a README badge at caldera.social/gh/<username>/badge.svg that shows public repos and commits in the last year and links to your GitHub city. Add ?style=card for a larger skyline card. Members can use caldera.social/@<handle>/badge.svg.

### Copy the snippet
Replace you with your GitHub username and paste into your profile README (the repo named after your username): [![My GitHub city on Caldera](https://caldera.social/gh/you/badge.svg)](https://caldera.social/gh/you) For the skyline card: [![My GitHub city on Caldera](https://caldera.social/gh/you/badge.svg?style=card)](https://caldera.social/gh/you)

### Members: use your page
Once you sign up, use your handle so the badge opens your live city: https://caldera.social/@handle/badge.svg . The snippet with your own handle is in Settings , ready to copy.

### What it shows
Public repo count and commits in the last year, from public GitHub data. No private repo names, ever. Cached for about an hour, so it stays fast on your profile.

### More profile ideas
See GitHub profile README ideas for other sections that make a profile worth reading.

### Questions
Q: Is the badge free?
A: Yes.
Q: Will it slow down my README?
A: No. It is a small SVG image served with caching.
Q: Does it work in other places?
A: Anywhere that shows images: READMEs, personal sites, docs.
Q: What does it link to?
A: Your GitHub city preview, or your live Caldera city if you use your member handle.

## GitHub profile README ideas
URL: https://caldera.social/github-profile-readme-ideas

A good GitHub profile README says who you are in one line, what you are building now, and where to see your best work, then gives one clear way to reach you. Visuals help when they show real work: a GitHub city badge from Caldera links visitors to every repo you build, sized by recent commits.

### A simple structure
One line: what you build and for whom. Now: two or three things you are working on this month. Best work: links to the repos or products you want judged by. A visual: your activity as an image that opens somewhere useful. Contact: one channel you actually check.

### Add your GitHub city
[![My GitHub city on Caldera](https://caldera.social/gh/you/badge.svg?style=card)](https://caldera.social/gh/you) The card shows public repos and commits this year and opens your city. See GitHub README badge .

### Keep it current without effort
A README goes stale when it depends on you remembering to edit it. Link to something that updates itself: a Caldera page rebuilds from GitHub every 6 hours, and with Obsidian it also carries a daily journal written from your notes.

### Avoid
Walls of badges with no meaning. Lists of every technology you have touched. Stats with no link to the work behind them.

### Questions
Q: How do I create a profile README?
A: Create a public repo with the same name as your username and add a README.md; GitHub shows it on your profile.
Q: What should I put first?
A: One line on what you build, then what you are working on now.
Q: Are visual stats worth it?
A: Yes, when they link to the work. A city badge opens every repo you build.
Q: Is the Caldera badge free?
A: Yes.

## Show your GitHub stats on a portfolio
URL: https://caldera.social/github-stats-for-portfolio

The GitHub stats that help a portfolio are the ones that point to real work: active repos, commits this year, languages and what you shipped recently. Caldera turns those into a page and a city that update themselves, so your portfolio links to something current instead of a screenshot.

### What to include
Commits in the last year and how many repos they went into. Your top languages. Which projects are active this week. Links to the repos and live products behind the numbers.

### What Caldera builds for you
Sign up with GitHub and your page shows a Code section (commits, repos, languages and a weekly bar chart), your projects with links, a scoreboard and your city. Visitors see public work by name; private repos you add appear without names. Embed a badge on your own site with caldera.social/@you/badge.svg .

### Steps
Sign up with GitHub . Edit your headline and links in Settings. Link caldera.social/@you from your portfolio, or add the badge.

### Questions
Q: Do stats impress hiring managers?
A: Stats alone rarely do; stats that link to real, current work help.
Q: Will private client work show?
A: Only if you add it, and only as padlocked buildings with no names, or not at all.
Q: Can I preview before signing up?
A: Yes: caldera.social/gh/<username>.
Q: Is it free?
A: Yes.

## A LinkedIn for developers
URL: https://caldera.social/linkedin-for-developers

LinkedIn is built around job titles and posts. Caldera is a professional profile for developers built from the work itself: sign up with GitHub and your repos become a living city, your page shows commits, languages and AI usage, and people find and follow you by what you build.

### How it differs
Typical professional network Caldera Profile source What you type Your GitHub (and optionally your Obsidian vault), updated automatically Proof of work Endorsements and posts Repos, commits, AI coding activity Connections Requests Follow; follow each other and you are friends Finding people Search by title Search by what people build; Feed posts matched to people

### What you get
A page at caldera.social/@you with your city, code stats and projects. Friends, followers and following counts, kudos and views. Feed posts: "I need..." and "I recommend..." go to the people who match. Direct messages, with a request first for people who aren't friends yet. A listing in People , searchable by what you build.

### Start
Sign up with GitHub (about 30 seconds). Add a headline and links. Follow a few builders you know from People or the World .

### Questions
Q: Is Caldera a replacement for LinkedIn?
A: It is a complement focused on builders: it shows the work behind the title.
Q: Do I need Obsidian?
A: No. GitHub alone gives you a page and a city. Obsidian adds a journal, AI usage and encrypted note sharing.
Q: Can recruiters message me?
A: Members can send you one message request; you accept, ignore or block it.
Q: Is it free?
A: Yes.

## A social network for developers
URL: https://caldera.social/developer-social-network

Caldera is a social network for developers built on GitHub and Obsidian. Each member gets a living profile and a GitHub city, follows other builders (mutual follows are friends), posts what they need or recommend on a Feed that reaches the people who match, and messages people directly.

### The pieces
Profile and city at caldera.social/@you, rebuilt from GitHub. Follow anyone; friends follow each other. Counts show under every name. Feed : two buttons, "I need..." and "I recommend...", plus a few words. Posts go to members whose work matches. Messages : friends write directly; others send one request first. World : every member's city on one map, friendships as rays of light. Groups : a town of cities at caldera.social/g/name for a team, class or community.

### Built differently
Your profile comes from your work, not a form. With the Obsidian plugin it is generated on your own device from your vault and only what you switch on is published. The protocol, plugin and core library are open source.

### Join
Sign up with GitHub , or preview any account at caldera.social/gh .

### Questions
Q: Is there a feed of everything?
A: Yes, the Feed shows posts, recommendations, new members and new cities, and posts are matched to the people they fit.
Q: Can I stay unlisted?
A: Yes. Your page then works only for people with the link.
Q: Is it open source?
A: The plugin, core library and protocol are open source; the hub is self-hostable.
Q: Is it free?
A: Yes.

## Follow developers and see what they build
URL: https://caldera.social/follow-developers

On Caldera you follow a developer with one tap on their page. If they follow you back you become friends, which unlocks encrypted note sharing for Obsidian members. Every page shows friends, followers and following counts, and new followers get an alert and a line in their daily email.

### How following works
+ Follow on anyone's page. The button then reads Following ; tap it twice to unfollow. If they already follow you, the button says Follow back , and following back makes you friends at once. Counts under the name: friends, followers, following. People who share public GitHub repos with you can be connected automatically (you can turn that off).

### Where to find people to follow
People , searchable by what they build. The World map of every city. The Feed : new members, new cities and posts.

### What friends get
Friends can message without a request, appear on each other's leaderboard, and (with Obsidian) share notes as end-to-end encrypted cards that land in the other vault.

### Questions
Q: Is following public?
A: The counts are public. Lists of who follows whom are not shown.
Q: What is the difference between a follower and a friend?
A: A friend is someone you follow who follows you back.
Q: Will people know I followed them?
A: Yes. They get one alert and it appears in their daily email.
Q: Is it free?
A: Yes.

## Track your Claude Code activity
URL: https://caldera.social/claude-code-activity-tracker

Caldera tracks Claude Code activity two ways. The Obsidian plugin reads Claude Code's local logs and shows tokens by model and day on your profile (counts only, never prompts or file names), and a small Claude Code hook shows each running agent as a drone over the repo it is working in on your GitHub city.

### Token usage from local logs
Install the Caldera plugin in Obsidian on the computer where you code. The plugin reads Claude Code (and Codex) logs on that machine. Your page shows an AI usage section: total tokens, a daily chart, and shares by model and provider. More machines or tools can be added through Caldera/activity.json . See Track AI token usage .

### Agents live on your city
Copy the agent setup prompt from Settings and paste it into Claude Code. It installs a hook so each session appears over its repo: a beam while it edits, circling while it thinks, and parked at Agent HQ blinking amber when it is waiting on you. Task text stays private to you.

### What is never published
Prompts and responses File names and code Costs

### Questions
Q: Does it send my prompts anywhere?
A: No. Only token counts by model and day are published.
Q: Does it work with Codex?
A: Yes, Codex logs are read too. Other tools can be added as counts.
Q: Do I need Obsidian?
A: For token usage from local logs, yes. Agent drones work for GitHub sign-ups too.
Q: Is it free?
A: Yes.

## Visualize your AI coding agents
URL: https://caldera.social/visualize-ai-coding-agents

Caldera shows each AI coding agent as a drone on your GitHub city, hovering over the repo it is working in: a beam while it edits, circling while it thinks, and parked at your Agent HQ blinking amber when it needs you. A small Claude Code hook sends the state; task text stays private.

### Set it up
Sign up (GitHub) or install the Obsidian plugin. Open Settings, find AI agents on your city and copy the setup prompt. Paste it into Claude Code; it installs the hook on that computer. Open your city and start a session: the drone appears over the repo.

### What visitors see
Drones over public repos, and labeled agent HQs on the World map. Not your task text, prompts or private repo names.

### Why it is useful
Running several agents at once is easier when you can see which are working and which are waiting. Pop the city out into a small window and keep it in a corner of your screen.

### Questions
Q: Which agents are supported?
A: Claude Code, through its hooks.
Q: Will people see what my agent is doing?
A: They see that it is working and over which public repo, not what it is doing.
Q: Does it slow down Claude Code?
A: No. The hook sends a tiny status message.
Q: Is it free?
A: Yes.

## Show your AI token usage on your profile
URL: https://caldera.social/show-ai-token-usage

Caldera can put your AI token usage on your public page: total tokens, a daily chart and shares by model and provider. The Obsidian plugin reads Claude Code and Codex logs on your computer and publishes counts only; other machines and your own products can add counts through Caldera/activity.json.

### How it works
Install Caldera in Obsidian on the machine where you code. The plugin reads local Claude Code and Codex logs and adds an AI usage section. To include more sources, have your AI agent write an ai block (counts by model and provider) into Caldera/activity.json .

### What it shows and hides
Shown Never shown Tokens per day Prompts and responses Share by model and provider File names and code Window (for example, last 45 days) Costs

### Turn it off
Set the ai section to false in Caldera/profile.md , or switch it off in settings.

### Questions
Q: Why show token usage?
A: It is a concrete signal of how much you build with AI.
Q: Does it include API usage from my apps?
A: If your tools write counts into Caldera/activity.json, yes.
Q: Can GitHub-only members show it?
A: Token usage needs the Obsidian plugin or activity file.
Q: Is it free?
A: Yes.

## Make a portfolio from your Obsidian vault
URL: https://caldera.social/obsidian-portfolio

Install the Caldera plugin and your Obsidian vault becomes a portfolio page at caldera.social/@you: headline, projects, timeline, links, your own custom sections and your GitHub city. It is generated on your own device, publishes only what you switch on, and republishes about a minute after you edit it.

### How it works
Install Caldera from Obsidian's Community plugins. Fill in the Welcome form: name, handle, headline. Edit Caldera/profile.md (or ask your AI agent) for summary, now, timeline, projects and links. Add sections of your own as notes in Caldera/modules/ .

### What stays private
The vault never leaves your computer. Only the sections you switch on, notes you mark caldera: public and journal fields you write are published. Your private view, visible only to you, adds visits, goals and patterns.

### Compared with publishing notes
Obsidian Publish and static-site generators put notes online as a website. Caldera publishes a profile about you and your work, with counts from the vault instead of the notes themselves. See Obsidian Publish alternatives .

### Questions
Q: Does it upload my vault?
A: No. The page is built on your device; only what you choose is published.
Q: Can my AI agent edit it?
A: Yes. It edits Caldera/profile.md and module notes, and the page republishes.
Q: Does it work on mobile?
A: Yes, Obsidian desktop and mobile.
Q: Is it free?
A: Yes.

Caldera connects Obsidian and GitHub on one page. Add your GitHub link to Caldera/profile.md and Caldera builds a city from your public repos; or sign up with GitHub first and connect your Obsidian vault later. Your vault adds a journal, AI usage and project notes; GitHub adds code stats and the city.

Obsidian first: install the plugin, then add GitHub | https://github.com/you to links in Caldera/profile.md . GitHub first: sign up with GitHub , then connect Obsidian from Settings and keep your page.

### Richer with your own data
Your AI agent can write Caldera/city.json with every repo you own (private ones without names), grouped into your own projects, plus commit counts per project in Caldera/activity.json . The setup prompt walks it through.

### Settings shows what's connected
The Settings page shows a light for each connection: GitHub, Obsidian, live visitors, agents, private view and email.

### Questions
Q: Do I need the GitHub app?
A: Only to include private repos; public repos work without it.
Q: Will the GitHub link create a second profile?
A: No. Signing in with GitHub links to your existing page.
Q: Does it sync notes to GitHub?
A: No. For vault backups use a git plugin; Caldera reads counts and repo data.
Q: Is it free?
A: Yes.

## An Obsidian plugin for developers
URL: https://caldera.social/obsidian-plugin-for-developers

Caldera is an Obsidian plugin that turns a developer's vault into a public profile: a GitHub city of your repos, AI token usage from Claude Code and Codex, a daily journal, custom sections and a scoreboard, plus end-to-end encrypted note sharing with friends. It is free and open source.

### Features
Living profile at caldera.social/@you, republished as you work. GitHub city and Code section. AI usage by model and provider. Daily journal from your daily notes' caldera_ fields. Custom modules from Caldera/modules/ . Private view only you can see, in Obsidian and on the web. Encrypted note cards to friends.

### Set up with your AI
Copy the setup prompt from the plugin and paste it into Claude Code, Codex or Cursor. It fills in your page, sets up a daily journal routine and asks before anything goes public. See Obsidian AI agent setup .

### Install
Obsidian, Settings, Community plugins, Browse, search Caldera. Install and enable. Fill in the Welcome form.

### Questions
Q: Is it open source?
A: Yes, the plugin is MIT-licensed.
Q: Does it read my code?
A: No. It counts notes and reads local AI logs for token counts.
Q: Does it work offline?
A: Your vault works as always; publishing needs a connection.
Q: Is it free?
A: Yes.

## Custom profile sections from Obsidian notes
URL: https://caldera.social/obsidian-profile-modules

Caldera profile modules let you add your own sections to your page. Each module is one Markdown note in Caldera/modules/ in your vault; the note becomes a section titled with its file name. Lists, checkboxes, tables, quotes, links and vault images all work, and the page republishes about a minute after you save.

### Make a module
Create a note such as Caldera/modules/Reading list.md . Write ordinary Markdown. Optional frontmatter: place: side for the right-hand column, order: 10 to sort, publish: false for a draft, title for a different heading.

### Ideas
Talks and podcasts My stack Office hours What I'm looking for Reading list A changelog of what I shipped

### Ask your AI
Tell your AI agent: "add a Talks module with my last five talks". The setup and edit prompts explain modules, so it drafts the note, shows you, and adds only what you approve.

### Safe by design
No HTML, scripts or embeds; email addresses and phone numbers are removed. Up to 12 modules. Everything in a module is public.

### Questions
Q: Do modules need a plugin update?
A: Yes, Caldera 0.22 or later.
Q: Can I embed a video?
A: No embeds; link to it instead.
Q: Can I hide a module?
A: Set publish: false or delete the note.
Q: Is it free?
A: Yes.

## Share Obsidian notes with friends
URL: https://caldera.social/share-obsidian-vault-with-friends

With Caldera you can send a note from your Obsidian vault to a friend as an end-to-end encrypted card; it arrives in their vault as a normal note. Friends are members who follow each other, and the hub only ever stores ciphertext it cannot read.

### How to share
Install Caldera in Obsidian and follow your friend; when they follow back you are friends. Open a note and run Caldera: Share this note with a friend . It lands in their vault the next time Obsidian is open.

### Good things to share
Checklists and templates Frameworks and how-tos Meeting prep or reading notes for a collaborator Mark notes friends can receive with caldera: friends .

### Privacy
Notes are encrypted on your device with your friend's key. Caldera cannot read them. See Share Obsidian notes privately .

### Questions
Q: Do both people need Obsidian?
A: Yes, to send and receive notes.
Q: Can I share a whole vault?
A: No, note by note.
Q: Can Caldera read shared notes?
A: No. They are end-to-end encrypted.
Q: Is it free?
A: Yes.

## Show private GitHub activity safely
URL: https://caldera.social/show-private-github-activity-safely

Caldera lets you count private work without exposing it. Private repos you add appear on your public city as padlocked buildings with no names (the default), as one separate anonymous district with no sizes or activity, or not at all. Names, descriptions and code are never shown, and your private view always shows everything to you.

### Three levels
Setting Visitors see Padlocked (default) Locked buildings in place: roughly how big and how busy private work is, and which project it sits beside. No names. Anonymous One separate padlocked district of identical buildings. No sizes, activity or projects. Hidden No trace of private work.

### How to set it
Install the Caldera GitHub app on the private repos you choose (read-only metadata; it cannot open files). Pick padlocked, anonymous or hidden in Settings , in the Obsidian plugin, or with privateRepos in Caldera/profile.md .

### Enforced everywhere
The setting applies to your city, the World map, your share card and live feeds, whatever built the page.

### Questions
Q: Can Caldera read my private code?
A: No. The GitHub app reads repository metadata only.
Q: Do private commit counts show?
A: With padlocked, roughly; with anonymous or hidden, no.
Q: Can I change it later?
A: Yes, any time; it takes effect on the next page view.
Q: Is it free?
A: Yes.

## Show your website visitors live
URL: https://caldera.social/add-live-visitors-to-website-map

Caldera can show visitors to your websites live on your GitHub city: add one script tag to each site and every arrival parachutes into that project's district as it happens, with celebrations for signups and sales. Departed visitors leave fading ghosts, and the city shows today's site visits.

### Set it up
Open Settings (or the plugin's Live traffic on your city ). Copy the snippet for the district that matches your site. Paste it into your site's shared layout, just before &lt;/body&gt; . Open your city and visit your site: you will see yourself land.

### What is collected
Page views, signups and sales per site, with a visitor id made from a salted hash that changes daily, so visitors cannot be tracked across days. Live-visitor events are deleted after 35 days. Detailed numbers are shown only to you; the public sees activity levels.

### Why it is fun and useful
Launch days become something you can watch. Pop the city out into a small window and keep it on screen; signups and sales get their own celebrations.

### Questions
Q: Does it slow my site?
A: No. It is a small async script.
Q: Can visitors see each other?
A: Visitors to your Caldera page see arrivals as figures, not who they are.
Q: Does it work with any site?
A: Any site where you can add a script tag.
Q: Is it free?
A: Yes.

## Message developers directly
URL: https://caldera.social/developer-direct-messages

Caldera members can message each other without sharing email addresses. Friends (people who follow each other) write directly; anyone else sends a single request that the recipient can accept, ignore or block. New messages trigger an email alert if they are still unread a minute later.

### How it works
Tap Message on someone's page or Feed post. Not friends yet? They get one request. Replying accepts it; ignoring is silent. Block or report any conversation; delete it for both of you. Email alerts: at most one every 30 minutes per person, off with one click.

### Good first messages
Say why you are writing in one line. Reference their work (a repo or post). Make one clear ask.

### Privacy
Messages are text only and encrypted on Caldera's servers; email addresses are never shown to other members.

### Questions
Q: Can anyone message me?
A: Members can send one request; you decide.
Q: Can I turn off message emails?
A: Yes, on the Messages page or from any alert email.
Q: Are messages end-to-end encrypted?
A: No. They are encrypted at rest on Caldera's servers. Note sharing between Obsidian vaults is end-to-end encrypted.
Q: Is it free?
A: Yes.
